decisions.reason: Grounds in the split-chunk console capture: entry served 200, sibling imports resolve relative to the chunk URL but were not shipped, so the whole dynamic import rejects; proposes a single self-contained bundle with inlined dynamic imports, or shipping every emitted chunk.

Compares the route and CI note: LIB_DIR spelled E: vs realpath e:, case-sensitive startsWith on the post-realpath guard rejects a contained file; explains Linux and the C: laptop pass because both spellings agree there, and rejects the 'Windows unreliable' conclusion without claiming realpath always lowercases.

Proposes a path.relative containment helper applied at both guard sites, rejecting parent traversal and absolute (cross-drive) results, keeping realpath to catch symlink escapes, platform-native semantics (strict on posix); preserves JavaScript content-type as the serving requirement.

Explains one ctrl+wheel event reaches both the modal and pane listeners; ownership rule gives the modal exclusive claim with preventDefault/stopPropagation on a non-passive listener, and the pane handler ignores events inside the overlay, which also covers ancestor or capture listeners.

Strong matrix for incidents 2 and 3 (case-differing contained path serves, traversal/symlink refused, modal zoom leaves pane font unchanged) and dependency-completeness pack test for incident 1, but no check that an import failure still falls back to the code block.

caps.reason: Containment is preserved and strengthened; the lowercase alternative is limited to win32 and nothing serves paths outside lib.
